newsitem.title: NIGER: Niger power workers arrested, supplies restored.
newsitem.headline: Niger power workers arrested, supplies restored.

text.p: Police in West African nation of Niger said on Saturday they had arrested at least 20 strikers from the state electricity company NIGELEC, some of them on charges of sabotaging the national grid.
Power supplies, cut off in some places for 72 hours by a wildcat strike against plans to privatise the company, were restored on Saturday.

The power workers union SYNATREN called an indefinite strike on Thursday of the 1,000 workers at NIGELEC to demand the release of about 10 union militants, arrested earlier in the dispute. The government says the strike was illegal.
Police sources said some of the workers arrested were accused of failing to provide a minimum service during an illegal strike.
The government of the impoverished state on the fringe of the Sahara desert plans to include NIGELEC among about a dozen companies to be privatised. The union opposes the plan.
The privatisation plan was is part of a structural adjustment programme agreed as a loan condition with the World Bank and International Monetary Fund.
